# Input otp

Separate boxes for a one-time code.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill">In Multi-brand</span></p>

## When to use it

**In Multi-brand:** The code that verifies an email or phone.

- **Use it when:** A short code sent by text or email, typed or pasted.
- **Not when:** Passwords or any value that is not a fixed-length code.

Instead:

- [Input](./input.md): Any other short value.

## Words

- Shared structure: object, state, next step.
- Brand tone lives in headlines and marketing copy, not in errors.
- Errors and confirmations read the same in every brand.
- Use: Get started, Plan, Order. Avoid: Brand-specific words in errors, Jargon.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Cancel
- `content.action.destroy`: Remove
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Get started

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

Test before you ship:

- [ ] Screen readers hear one field with a label, and pasting the whole code works. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add input-otp
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Tokens it reads

Input otp reads 16 tokens of its own, each an alias of a semantic token. Each row is one part: its own token, the semantic it aliases, and the value it ends at. Change a semantic and every component that reads it follows; override one of Input otp's tokens to change Input otp alone.
